baseline: Known unmodified DOS 1.0 and Windows 1.0 Capitalism Plus builds

entries.title: Town records contain pointer-like runtime residue
entries.observed_behavior: Two 32-bit town-record fields differ across the matched DOS and Windows saves like transient runtime values. Their pointer interpretation remains inferred, and normalization is limited to the registered byte ranges.
entries.notes: Original-save import may classify the registered bytes under the versioned normalization policy. Canonical runtime state and native saves must never store host pointers or object addresses.

entries.title: Town market floats drift across builds
entries.observed_behavior: The matched saves contain 370 changed values among four tracked float32 positions, and every changed value is one to four ULPs apart across the two builds.
entries.notes: The economic meanings and arithmetic path still need controlled probes. Choose a canonical result only after establishing whether the drift changes decisions.

entries.title: Terrain fertility has a compiler signed-char divergence
entries.observed_behavior: For a negative interior base-land fertility intermediate, the DOS path clamps to 100 while the Windows path clamps to 0 because the compiler-generated byte comparisons use different signedness.
entries.notes: The inspector exposes both original profiles. Measure the gameplay consequence before selecting the deterministic Classic rule.
